decisions.reason: Changing the spout geometry to preserve beverage quality does not alter the existing leak-prevention requirements.
The source changes spout geometry and adds a froth-preservation constraint but does not change the valve mechanism, closed-valve behavior, or controlled-flow criteria.
The requested spout shape and beverage-quality constraint do not change the established removability, flushing, or cleaning requirements.
The source concerns the downstream spout and does not modify bowl capacity, depth, or form.
The existing mixing-quality target remains unchanged; the source separately requires the spout to preserve the consistency and frothiness already produced.
The spout modification does not affect the machine name or retained placard wording.
The source does not change whisk dimensions, bowl compatibility, or suitability for fine matcha powder.
The spout geometry decision does not alter the requirement for rapid bowl removal and swapping.
The source addresses consistency and frothiness during dispensing, not splash behavior during mixing.
Although the revised spout may inform later component selection, the source does not change the BOM deliverable or its stated selection goal.
The source does not revise the V1 speed priority or the policy of using off-the-shelf components where practical.
The requested spout geometry and beverage-quality behavior do not change the beige and green color scheme.
